title: Brucie Flattens the Commish While Philly's New Toys Score 35.6 and Sonny's Score Zero
dek: No Banner only HULK posted the week's best score by 27 points in the main event, Team Pillbert won its fifth straight with the players it pried from Sonny, and the race for the fourth playoff spot is now a four-team brawl.
body: The main event was not close. Ramon's No Banner only HULK beat Sonny's The Horse is Hea 134.4 to 102.58, with the commish going in as a 33% home underdog and coming out with a 31.82-point loss. Brucie's backfield did the damage: Kenneth Walker III posted 26.9 on a 21.85 projection and Christian McCaffrey added 26.2 on a 19.15 projection, a combined 53.1 from two running backs. That 134.4 was the best score of the week by 27.34 points, and No Banner only HULK now has 829.4 points on the season, 97.8 more than anyone else. Ramon wasn't sure he wanted to be in this league, and now he's lapping it.

Sonny had a good game from James Cook III, who scored 22.8 on an 18.53 projection, but the rest of the afternoon hurt. Both players he just got from Alan sat on his bench, where George Pickens scored 10.3 and Ollie Gordon II scored zero, and Bryce Young added 19.84 from the bench too. The commish also did some housecleaning, dropping Jalen Hurts, adding Jameson Williams, swapping Juwan Johnson for Pat Freiermuth, and cutting the Bears D/ST for the 49ers D/ST. A Chicago guy cutting the Bears defense for a West Coast team is the kind of thing that happens after a few years of Boston winters. His title odds fell from 18% to 11%, but at 4-2 he still has an 86% chance at the playoffs.

Meanwhile, the bad guy keeps winning. Alan's Team Pillbert beat Randy's The fumblers 107.06 to 85.5 as a 59% favorite, and the stars were the two players Philly got from Sonny: Chuba Hubbard scored 18.6 and DeVonta Smith added 17 in their first starts, a combined 35.6. Javonte Williams chipped in 12 more, while Justin Jefferson didn't start and didn't score. That's five straight wins, a 5-1 record matching Ramon's, and title odds at 26%, up from 16% a week ago. Philly also kept the waiver wire busy: Josh Jacobs, Tank Dell, Brenton Strange, and Dameon Pierce came in, while Tyreek Hill and Odell Beckham Jr. went out, Beckham a week after he arrived.

Randy has now lost three straight, and this one came with a painful bench. Derrick Henry managed 4.5 on a 17.6 projection, while Trevor Lawrence scored 27.34 on the bench and Stefon Diggs added 13.4 there too, all in a 21.56-point loss. The fumblers' 85.5 was the second-lowest score of the week. Randy swapped the Raiders D/ST for the Rams D/ST and cut kicker Brandon Aubrey. He's still fourth at 3-3, but the model puts his playoff odds at 34%, behind two teams at 2-4, which says plenty about how it views his last three weeks.

Mekhi's Dawgs beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 105.6 to 83.44 as the road favorite, and Kai's waiver work led the way. Malik Nabers, last week's pickup, posted 22.5 on a 14.6 projection, and Ashton Jeanty added 13.8, which made up for Kyren Williams scoring 8.2 on a 19.17 projection. The twist: Tyler Shough, who scored negative 0.16 as Kai's starting quarterback last week, sat on the bench this week and scored 26.96. Mekhi won anyway, and he kept shopping, grabbing the Ravens D/ST and kicker Dominic Zvada. For Zilgit, it was Bijan Robinson's day to disappear: 6.3 points on a 21.34 projection, with an 83.44 team total that was the week's lowest. She did make the boldest move of the week, dropping Lamar Jackson and adding Jordan Love, which is about as Wisconsin as a roster decision can get.

Kaushal's Habibsters beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 100.5 to 92.72 as a 70% favorite, and Habib's new quarterback made it look easy. Drake Maye, picked up for Sam Darnold this week, scored 23.8 on a 20.25 projection in his first start. Kaushal was the wire's busiest shopper: Tony Pollard and Juwan Johnson, both cut by Sonny in the last two weeks, joined, Woody Marks came in for Keenan Allen and then left for Pollard, the Chiefs D/ST arrived, and Rome Odunze and Rico Dowdle went out. JMoney got 22.7 from Bhayshul Tuten on an 11.69 projection and 20.9 from Isaiah Likely, but Emeka Egbuka scored 14.3 on the bench while Denzel Boston started and scored 2. That 12.3-point gap was bigger than the 7.78-point margin of defeat. Jordan is 1-5, and the model puts his playoff odds at 0%.

The standings now have two 5-1 teams at the top and a pile-up beneath them. No Banner only HULK is the favorite at 50%, oddly down from 55% after a 32-point win, because Team Pillbert climbed to 26% right behind it. The Horse is Hea sits third at 4-2 with 11%. Then it gets messy: The fumblers hold the fourth spot at 3-3 but have the worst playoff odds of the group at 34%, while Habibsters (41%) and Dawgs (36%) are 2-4 and lurking, and Ghostu-Spider SZN is hanging on at 5%. With eight regular-season weeks left, that fourth playoff spot is wide open.

Week 7 has stakes all over the board. Randy hosts Sonny in a game the fumblers badly need, and the commish needs one to keep pace with the 5-1 teams. Mekhi and Kaushal meet in a 2-4 showdown where the loser's playoff odds will take a serious hit. Zoe gets Team Pillbert and five straight wins, and Ramon draws JMoney, who would love nothing more than to dent the league's best team. The two 5-1 teams don't meet this week, so expect them to stay tied at the top unless somebody has an off day.

social.author: Hulk Smash Society
social.text: 134.4. Walker 26.9. CMC 26.2. The commissioner can control the website. He cannot control our running backs.

social.author: Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Sources confirm someone needs to tell Brucie his title odds went DOWN after a 32-point win. Sources also recommend putting the controller somewhere safe first.

social.author: Pillbert Truthers
social.text: Hubbard 18.6. Smith 17. Five straight. Thank you, Commish, for your generous contribution to the cause. The model says 26%. We say it's just getting started.

social.author: The Hea Hive
social.text: Pickens 10.3 on the bench, Gordon 0, Bryce Young 19.84 also on the bench. 4-2 and 86% playoff odds. We're fine. We're totally fine. Randy, see you Sunday.

social.author: Fumblers Faithful
social.text: Henry 4.5. Lawrence 27.34 on the bench. Diggs 13.4 on the bench. Three straight losses and we're still in fourth. Somehow the standings like us more than the model does.

social.author: Kai's Waiver Desk
social.text: Nabers off the wire: 22.5. Shough on the bench: 26.96. Win is a win. The king of the wire keeps the crown. Habib, you're next.

social.author: Habib Highway Patrol
social.text: Clocked Drake Maye at 23.8 in a brand new uniform. We'd write him a ticket but Kaushal knows how those go. 2-4 and 41% playoff odds, best of the bottom four.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider Silk Society
social.text: Bijan 6.3 on a 21.34 projection. We dropped Lamar for Jordan Love and we regret nothing. Green and gold runs through this web. Philly, bring a coat.

social.author: Two-Minute Toby
social.text: Egbuka on the bench: 14.3. Boston in the lineup: 2. Margin of defeat: 7.78. JMoney, the numbers were right there. You of all people should have counted them.

trade_watch.take: One week in, it already looks as lopsided as the model said. Hubbard and Smith both started and scored 35.6 for Alan in a win, while Pickens (10.3) and Gordon (0) sat on Sonny's bench during a 31-point loss.

Hubbard has 44 points since this deal, and none of them came for Sonny; his 18.6 this week went to Alan instead. Rice is still at zero for Ramon, so neither original side has gotten anything out of it, and the real winner turned out to be a third team.

Likely keeps paying off for JMoney with 20.9 more and 47.8 since the deal, but Egbuka's 14.3 on the bench while Boston started for 2 cost him a game he lost by 7.78. Jordan still clearly won this trade on paper; using it is another matter.

This keeps getting worse for Randy: Javonte added 12 for a Pillbert win and is up to 54 points since the deal. Diggs scored 13.4 on the fumblers' bench in a loss and has only 6 lineup points for Randy.

Adams and Jeanty are up to 48 points for Mekhi against Jefferson's 15.8, and Jefferson didn't start or score this week. Both teams won, so Kai still leads the box score and Alan still leads the standings.

bios.1: The commish is 4-2 after Ramon put up 134 on him, and his title odds slid from 18% to 11%. His new trade pieces haven't cracked the lineup yet, but 86% playoff odds still give him plenty of room. A trip to Randy's place is next.
bios.2: Randy is 3-3 and holding fourth place, but he's lost three straight and the model only gives him 34% playoff odds. Derrick Henry's 4.5 and Trevor Lawrence's 27.34 on the bench summed up the week. The Sonny game is close to a must-win.
bios.3: JMoney is 1-5, and the model has his playoff odds at 0% with eight weeks left. Tuten and Likely scored 43.6 together, but a benched Egbuka cost him a winnable game. Ramon's juggernaut is next, so spoiler season starts now.
bios.4: Alan has won five straight and is 5-1, and the players he got from Sonny scored 35.6 in their first start. The title odds jumped to 26%, second-best in the league, and Philly still won't stop working the waiver wire. Zoe is next on the schedule.
bios.5: Kai is 2-4 after a comfortable win over Zoe, led by waiver pickup Malik Nabers' 22.5. The 36% playoff odds keep him in the race, but leaving Shough's 26.96 on the bench shows the lineup calls still need work. Habib is next in a playoff-race showdown.
bios.6: Kaushal is 2-4 but has the fourth-most points in the league, and new quarterback Drake Maye scored 23.8 in his debut. The 41% playoff odds are the best of any team under .500. The Dawgs game next week could decide who chases fourth place.
bios.7: Ramon's team is 5-1 and leads the league with 829.4 points, nearly 98 more than anyone else, after a 134.4-point win over the commish. Walker and McCaffrey are carrying the load, and the title odds sit at 50% even after a five-point dip. JMoney is up next.
bios.8: Zoe has lost two straight and sits at 2-4 with 5% playoff odds after Bijan Robinson managed only 6.3. The rookie made a bold move anyway, swapping Lamar Jackson for Jordan Love. Five-straight Pillbert is next, a chance to play spoiler.
